Header: Pseudocercospora griseola Amabara y’inguni/Kibogo in Kinyarwanda

Prevention: Use certified seeds (RAB, seed multipliers, agrodealers)
Avoid moving in the field when it is wet
Crop rotation practice with cereals (like maize) and tubers (like potato) for 2 seasons
RAB (RWV3006, RWV 3316, RWV 3317, MAC 44, RWV1129, RWR2154)
Monitoring: Monitor for symptoms of angular spots on leaves and large oval to circular spots on pods, once a week.
Symptoms include brown angular spots on leaves and pods
Consider taking action when 5% of plants with angular spot detected
Direct Control: Uproot heavily (large sporulating and coalescing regions, premature defoliation) infected plants to prevent further spread
Restrictions: Do not eat or drink while manipulating pesticides.
Unlikely to present acute hazards in normal use (WHO Class

U); Contact protectant fungicide; Do not harvest for 7 days after application; Spray when leaves, flowers or pods on plants first show signs of infection and weather conditions are likely to remain humid or wet and favour disease development; If disease pressure is severe and conditions favour spread of disease, repeat sprays at 2 to 3 weeks to protect new growth and developing pods.
